The leading digit is $a_N(x)=x-1006$, so $a_N(0)=-1006$. The reasoning only needs the degrees and the top two coefficients.

**Degree of the leading digit.** Each digit has degree at most 1, so $a_k b^k$ has degree at most $2k+1$. The polynomial has degree 2015 and $b^k$ has degree $2k$, so $N=1007$ and $a_N$ has degree exactly 1. Write $a_N(x)=cx+d$.

**Which terms affect the top coefficients.** Every term with $k\le N-1$ has degree at most $2(N-1)+1=2013$. So the coefficients of $x^{2015}$ and $x^{2014}$ in the polynomial come only from $a_N b^N$.

**Expanding the top term.** We have
$$b^{1007}=(x^2+x+1)^{1007}=x^{2014}+1007\,x^{2013}+\cdots$$
Hence
$$(cx+d)\,b^{1007}=c\,x^{2015}+(1007c+d)\,x^{2014}+\cdots$$

**Matching coefficients.** The polynomial $x^{2015}+x^{2014}+\cdots+1$ has coefficient 1 on both $x^{2015}$ and $x^{2014}$. This gives $c=1$ and $1007+d=1$, so $d=-1006$.

ANSWER: -1006
